scope: Qualification window only, RTX 4090 lane. The candidate is an unreleased build of the runtime fork's port/native-lanes-on-mainline branch installed in its own lineage state root (qwen38-4090-native); the shipped native components (v0.2.3-qwen38-4090-durable.1, v0.2.5-qwen38-3090-beta.1) were never started or modified. The RTX 3090 lane is not in this window: its host is unavailable until about 2026-09-21 (owner constraint), so the 3090 mainline candidate stays uncut and its shipped v0.2.5 component carries unchanged.
question: With the release path's five blockers closed (EXP-026), does the RTX 4090 mainline candidate pass its own lifecycle qualification end to end, and what do the phases that had never run expose?
answer: The phases beyond protocol ran for the first time and exposed two defects, both fixed and re-proven: an admission invariant that refused a legitimate request under Host StateImage pressure, and a restart phase that could not observe durability because nothing published the session it restarted. Running the registered suite with the artifact exported found a third - a publication-order race that let a consumer see its own completed request as live - fixed and proven red-to-green on real rebuilds. The candidate 075d442e passed 15/15 lane phases and 101/101 registered tests with the artifact.

defects_fixed.supersedes: the materialization-source-eviction open finding of 2026-09-09, whose stated cause (last replica evicted) was inference from the same conflated predicate and is corrected here
defects_fixed.symptom: At --host-state-slots 8 the agent protocol's request 10 (continue the surviving descendant after its parent Responses record is deleted) returned HTTP 500; the server logged 'materialization source has no resident state'. Reproduced in 34 s on the installed candidate.
defects_fixed.cause: prepare_materialization asked resident_resources(source) whether the planned source still had state. That function reports only what an owner holds exclusively - its exact transition effect - so a state another sequence also references contributes zero. Instrumenting the assertion on the failing request recorded: anchors=1 retained=0 endpoint=0 read==write=1 kv=1 read=invalid write=invalid anchor=res2/ref2/own1 - the continuation's endpoint had been retired and its remaining reuse source was a HostOnly long anchor with two checkpoint references against one owned, the ordinary shape after a sibling fork. Admission had legitimately planned private_long_anchor reuse from it.
defects_fixed.fix: aef33996 asserts on the selected source's replica residency, the question the planner itself asks (request_plan_impl.h: selected_state plus state_store->residency).

before.request_10: HTTP 500 materialization source has no resident state

defects_fixed.class_closure: The only other uses of resident_resources() are effect accounting (pressure option effects, the planner's final_removed, and the post-materialization entitlement equality), where exclusive ownership is the correct measure; the guard was the single place using it as a residency question. A pressure_protocol qualification phase now runs the same protocol against the installed release at eight Host StateImage slots, so the class cannot reach a candidate window unobserved again.

defects_fixed.symptom: The restart phase failed: the post-restart continuation returned HTTP 404. The session checkpoint root held zero files after the restart.
defects_fixed.cause: The phase seeded a ~40-token session and restarted, expecting the continuation to resolve. Nothing had published that session: automatic saves start at 32,768 frontier tokens (kDefaultSessionCheckpointMinTokens), and the shutdown flush in apps/serve/main.cpp runs only when listen() returns from a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler, which a Windows managed stop never delivers. The shipped native lanes pass this phase only because their qualification restarts a 102K-token session, which clears the automatic gate.
defects_fixed.fix: dac505de publishes the session through the documented explicit endpoint (POST /v1/ninfer/checkpoints), verifies the generation became available, and requires the post-restart continuation to quote the marker with a nonzero cached-token count. The phase also records restart wall time, so a slow managed start is data rather than an opaque timeout.
defects_fixed.evidence_integrity: The same commit drops five fields the phase's receipt asserted as 'passed' without ever exercising them (middle_delete_restart_regression, latest_delete_nonrestorable_regression, standalone_delete_nonrestorable_regression, durable_only_lru_delete_regression, post_commit_sync_regression).

open_findings.severity: durability gap, pre-existing on both native Windows lanes
open_findings.observation: HttpServer::save_all_checkpoints() (src/serve/http_server.cpp) drains the automatic queue and saves every live session, and apps/serve/main.cpp calls it after listen() returns. listen() returns only via server.stop() from the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler. Windows never raises SIGTERM, the managed server has no console to receive SIGINT, and Control-Release.ps1's Stop-ManagedProcess stops the scheduled task and then calls Stop-Process -Force. The flush is therefore unreachable on the native lanes. Measured: after two managed restarts of a live session, the checkpoint root held zero files.
open_findings.consequence: A session below the 32,768-token automatic-checkpoint gate that was never saved explicitly does not survive a deliberate stop. Sessions above the gate, and any session saved explicitly, do survive - that is what both shipped native lanes qualified.
open_findings.status: open, unchanged by this window. The RTX 5090 container lane is unaffected: docker stop delivers SIGTERM and the flush runs.
open_findings.not_fixed_here: A graceful-stop channel is new control surface on a serving process and belongs in its own reviewed change, not in a release candidate.

defects_fixed_after_the_window.found_by: ninfer_qwen3_6_27b_prefix_real_test, run for the first time on this host with the artifact exported
defects_fixed_after_the_window.symptom: exercise_concurrent_resource_settlement: after eight staggered rows each return their expected token count and OutputLimit, runtime_stats() still reports running=1 and terminal_pending=1.
defects_fixed_after_the_window.cause: A publication-order race between the engine and its consumer, not a leaked slot. commit_pending marks a terminal row ModelFinished and run_decode_round publishes statistics with the slot still occupied; on the next boundary settle_terminal_requests delivered the result - waking the waiter - before it released the lane and republished. wait() returned and read the stale snapshot. The same order existed in cancel_active_requests and the cancelled-terminal loop of commit_pending.
defects_fixed_after_the_window.fix: 075d442e splits completion into finalize and deliver and retires a lane in the order finalize, release, publish, deliver at every site that releases one.
